name: MeetRecord
tagline: Call recording, coaching, scorecards, and CRM-linked revenue intelligence

pricing.basis: paid plan; billing basis requires review
pricing.native: Public paid plan exists; amount not safely recovered
pricing.notes: The official pricing URL is recorded, but a stable current amount was not safely recoverable in this pass. Do not publish a number until rechecked.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: 60 minutes of roleplay/coaching credits; unlimited team members.
tiers.notes: The former MeetRecord pricing URL now redirects to Outdoo, a roleplay and coaching product rather than the meeting-recording product described on file.

tiers.name: Revenue Intelligence Free
tiers.limits: Unlimited Revenue Intelligence usage; the public page does not state a numeric team-member or storage cap.
tiers.notes: Separate Outdoo product from the metered roleplay/coaching credits.

tiers.name: Flex
tiers.limits: Usage-based roleplay/coaching plan with unlimited team members; public per-minute price is not stated.
tiers.notes: Annual contracts are standard; multi-year contracts are available.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Custom usage, security, implementation, and support package; no public numeric limits or price.

pricing.freeTierCaps: 60 roleplay/coaching minutes plus a separate Revenue Intelligence Free offer with unlimited usage; unlimited team members on the roleplay workspace.
pricing.billingTerms: usage-based annual contract; multi-year contracts available
pricing.hiddenCosts: Usage is billed separately from implementation; optional professional services are separately scoped. The live product no longer matches the meeting-recording description on file.

verdictSummary: Do not mistake the interface for the product. MeetRecord's durable value is capture, integrations, reliability, which a solo one-shot build cannot reproduce responsibly. The prompt therefore builds only the closest honest personal consolation tool.
coreLoopDIY: Build a private revenue meeting intelligence pipeline that accepts an audio file, transcribes it, creates structured notes, and exports Markdown.
diyTimeEstimate: not a true replacement; consolation build in one to two days
replacementScope: consolation build only; the paid product's moat remains
requirements: local Whisper model or optional API key in .env
Explicit README warning that this is a consolation build, not a production replacement
whyPeopleStillPay: MeetRecord: Customers pay for automatic capture, dependable speaker handling, search across calls, and notes arriving without manual file wrangling.
ongoingBurden: Own audio capture permissions, diarization quality, model downloads, storage, privacy, and integrations.

priorArt.name: whisper.cpp
priorArt.desc: Local speech-to-text engine suitable for private transcription.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Fathom
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The free plan records calls; coaching scorecards, CRM workflows and revenue intelligence are another product tier.

rejectedAlternatives.name: tl;dv
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Free transcripts are not free sales coaching: scorecards, CRM sync and playbooks are paid.

notes: Credibility row: MeetRecord survives for a structural reason, not because its interface is difficult to copy.
prompt:
Build the closest honest consolation tool inspired by MeetRecord; do not claim to replace its structural moat.
Use exactly this stack: Python 3.12 + FastAPI + whisper.cpp + SQLite.
Primary job: Build a private revenue meeting intelligence pipeline that accepts an audio file, transcribes it, creates structured notes, and exports Markdown.
Start from an empty folder and create the complete working project.
Make the default mode single-user and private.
Store user data locally unless the core job requires the declared self-hosted database.
Do not add analytics, telemetry, ads, or third-party accounts.
Put every secret and external credential in .env and provide .env.example.
Use realistic sample data that is clearly labelled and easy to delete.
Implement the smallest polished interface that completes the core loop end to end.
Include clear empty, loading, validation, success, and failure states.
Add import and export so the user is not trapped in the app.
Use accessible keyboard navigation, labels, focus states, and sensible contrast.
Validate untrusted input and never log secrets or private file contents.
Deliberately exclude these paid-product advantages: calendar and CRM integrations; cross-call team analytics; meeting-bot auto-join.
Do not fake integrations, network effects, proprietary data, model quality, compliance, or security claims.
Where an external API is optional, keep the app useful without it and explain the degraded mode.
Write focused unit tests for the data model and the most important workflow.
Add one end-to-end smoke test that proves the core loop works.
Create a README with setup, permissions, architecture, data location, backup, and limitations.
Add scripts for install, development, test, build, and a production-style local run.
Run the tests and build before finishing, then fix errors rather than merely describing them.
